newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED CAN GO SEVEN POINTS CLEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED CAN GO SEVEN POINTS CLEAR.

text.p: Manchester United turn their attention from Europe to the domestic league at the weekend while some of the country's unsung sides contest the quarter-finals of an extraordinary F.A. Cup competition.
League leaders United follow up Wednesday's 4-0 rout of Porto in the European Cup with a Saturday visit to Sunderland, themselves victims of a 4-0 midweek defeat by Tottenham.

If United win, as their stunning recent form and their 5-0 defeat of Sunderland earlier in the season suggests, they will go seven points clear at least until Monday when second-placed Liverpool host Newcastle.

The corresponding fixture at Anfield last season turned out to be a classic, with Liverpool eventually triumphing 4-3 thanks to an injury-time goal from Stan Collymore after Newcastle had led 2-1 and 3-2.

Liverpool enter Monday's match boosted by a valuable away draw at Norway's Brann Bergen in the Cup Winners' Cup. Newcastle, still without key striker Alan Shearer, look to recover from their 1-0 home UEFA Cup defeat by Monaco.
Slip-ups by any of the three northern giants could allow third-placed Arsenal back into the title race.
The Londoners, who entertain Nottingham Forest on Saturday, may give 17-year-old Nicolas Anelka his first-team debut following his controversial transfer from Paris St Germain earlier this year.
In the F.A. Cup, Chesterfield take on Wrexham on Sunday to decide who will become the first side from outside the top two divisions to reach the semifinals since 1984.
Chesterfield, in the last eight for the first time in their 131-year history, beat Forest in the last round. Wrexham have already eliminated West Ham and Birmingham.

Cup favourites Chelsea face a tricky tie at Portsmouth, unbeaten in their last seven first division matches and conquerors of Leeds in the fifth round of a competition which has continued to throw up surprises.
Chelsea player-manager Ruud Gullit has been sidelined by a cracked ankle bone and Gianluca Vialli is likely to claim an increasingly rare place in the starting line-up on Sunday.
Two of the premier league's in-form sides face each other in the cup at Hillsborough on Sunday.

Sheffield Wednesday, seeking their first F.A. Cup win since 1935, have lost just once in their last 22 matches. Their opponents Wimbledon, suprise cup winners in 1988, have lost only four of their last 36.
In the other quarter-final, Middlesbrough face Derby on Saturday, four days after they hammered them 6-1 in the league.
